correctness.rationale: For any positive period-six orbit, the six linear equations with coefficients 5 raised to nonnegative integer exponents have a nontrivial kernel. An exact Leibniz expansion gives the weighted six-cycle independent-set determinant. Modulo five, only 12 division supports survive; the no-division and all-division cases are separately excluded. The normalized independent-set sum is strictly decreasing in each divided coefficient and is already one at exponent one, so all positive exponents must equal one. Two cyclic support classes each have a one-dimensional rational kernel, with explicit primitive generators and direct valid valuations. The parity recurrence excludes nonmultiples of three; a maximum-entry argument excludes period three. The standalone standard-library verifier replayed exact determinant coefficients, 12 supports, matrix ranks and both trajectories. No finite data are treated as proof of an unbounded statement.

originality.rationale: Avila--Khovanova (2014), Section 9, exhibits the same two primitive cycles and explicitly leaves whether more exist unresolved. Its Lemma 28 provides only the period-divisibility condition, not exhaustion at period six. The new theorem does not claim discovery of those cycles, but classifies every positive six-cycle for unbounded seeds and valuation exponents. OEIS A214684 records only the first seeded cycle. Targeted equivalent, broader, and table searches found no decisive complete classification; this is not asserted to establish global uniqueness across all literature.
residual_risks: An unlocated later work or a general cyclic-division recurrence theorem might establish the same period-six completeness indirectly.
The result does not resolve whether primitive five-free cycles of least period greater than six exist.

value.rationale: The smallest base known to support both division-free infinite growth and positive recurrent cycles has two explicit primitive six-cycles known since 2014, but their uniqueness at the shortest possible period was not established in the inspected source. The theorem completely resolves that natural first-period classification over all unbounded positive seeds and arbitrarily large potential valuations. The determinant/independence-polynomial obstruction explains structural exhaustion rather than merely extending a computational table. No claim is made about all longer cycles.
